- 2-3 green/yellow-green seeds (appearing smaller/lighter than normal mature seeds)
- White fluffy/cottony material lining the inside of the pod walls

**Comparison across 7 reference classes viewed:**

- **Phomopsis**: Dried/shriveled dark seeds in mature brown pods — doesn't match (test seeds are green and plump)
- **Purple_Seed_Stain**: Distinctive purple staining on seed coat — not present
- **Green_stem_disorder**: Green stems persisting — irrelevant to pod interior
- **Tobacco_Streak_Virus**: Dark spots on pod exterior — not matching
- **Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus**: Black mottling on seed coat — not present
- **Anthracnose**: Dark irregular lesions on pod surface — not matching

The white cottony/fluffy material inside the pod, combined with the smaller/lighter green seeds, is the hallmark of White Mold infection inside pods.
